Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
input.rationale: Transition continuity is well covered and in fact exceeds the preferred position: Section 11.3 and Section 5.3 make our license to serve then-existing Customers and Commerce One's support and maintenance obligations survive termination indefinitely (subject to fee payment), and Section 12 adds a source code escrow. However, the exit provisions contain no data return: Section 11.3 only requires each party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at Commerce One's election, with no obligation to return data of Corio, its Customers or Software Users held on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification. Because the fallback requires a data export within 30 days and the current wording permits outright destruction of our data (walk-away territory), this fails the fallback on a material term. We propose a narrow insert (new Section 11.4) requiring return within 30 days in a machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification, together with the preferred six-month transition assistance at then-current rates; the assistance period can drop to 90 days as a fallback.

input.quote: A. No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, volume quota or take-or-pay obligation on Corio, so it meets the preferred position that fees are payable only for usage or ordered services. Exhibit B charges Corio a license fee, an annual MarketSite.net access fee and an annual maintenance fee for services actually received, plus a revenue share calculated as a percentage of Application Management Revenue Corio actually invoices (p0157), and implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped by the Statement of Work (p0161) - all consumption- or order-based rather than guaranteed spend. The only "minimum" (p0158) is a 40-user threshold that conditions a revenue-share waiver in Corio's favour; it does not obligate Corio to buy anything and is therefore not a commitment we would resist. Likewise the sole "shortfall" reference (p0059) is a reciprocal audit true-up - "the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment" - which is precisely the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers over a penalty, and it runs both ways. Exhibit D's sales and marketing items are expressly "non-binding," and the initial-customers item (p0205) is only a commercially reasonable efforts undertaking, not a purchase or volume commitment. Two points noted but not flagged: maintenance is structured so that continuation is conditioned on Corio electing to keep paying ("provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees," p0055), which preserves a practical exit rather than locking in five years of fees; and the five-year initial term has no termination-for-convenience right, but that is a term/termination issue outside this rule and would duplicate another rule's commercial term.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text: The document contains no take-or-pay obligation on Corio. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: A. No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, volume quota or take-or-pay obligation on Corio, so it meets the preferred position that fees are payable only for usage or ordered services. Exhibit B charges Corio a license fee, an annual MarketSite.net access fee and an annual maintenance fee for services actually received, plus a revenue share calculated as a percentage of Application Management Revenue Corio actually invoices (p0157), and implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped by the Statement of Work (p0161) — all consumption- or order-based rather than guaranteed spend. The only "minimum" (p0158) is a 40-user threshold that conditions a revenue-share waiver in Corio's favour; it does not obligate Corio to buy anything and is therefore not a commitment we would resist. Likewise the sole "shortfall" reference (p0059) is a reciprocal audit true-up — "the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment" — which is precisely the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers over a penalty, and it runs both ways. Exhibit D's sales and marketing items are expressly "non-binding," and the initial-customers item (p0205) is only a commercially reasonable efforts undertaking, not a purchase or volume commitment. Two points noted but not flagged: maintenance is structured so that continuation is conditioned on Corio electing to keep paying ("provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees," p0055), which preserves a practical exit rather than locking in five years of fees; and the five-year initial term has no termination-for-convenience right, but that is a term/termination issue outside this rule and would duplicate another rule's commercial term.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, TRANSITION).**

What I found:
- **Transition assistance — exceeds preferred.** Section 11.3 makes our right to serve then-existing Customers survive indefinitely, and Section 5.3/11.3 make Commerce One's support and maintenance obligations survive termination (subject to our annual fees). Section 12's source code escrow adds further continuity. No redline needed here.
- **Data return — fails the fallback.** The only exit data provision is the mutual Confidential Information clause in 11.3, which lets Commerce One elect to *destroy* our information, with no return obligation for data of Corio, its Customers or Software Users held on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification. Permitting outright destruction of our data sits in walk-away territory.

Redline (validated, ok:true): a single narrow insert of new Section 11.4 requiring (a) up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, (b) return of our and our Customers' data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and (c) deletion thereafter with written certification, subject to legal retention — with a stated willingness to fall back to 90 days of assistance.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Transition continuity is well covered and in fact exceeds the preferred position: Section 11.3 and Section 5.3 make our license to serve then-existing Customers and Commerce One's support and maintenance obligations survive termination indefinitely (subject to fee payment), and Section 12 adds a source code escrow. However, the exit provisions contain no data return: Section 11.3 only requires each party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at Commerce One's election, with no obligation to return data of Corio, its Customers or Software Users held on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification. Because the fallback requires a data export within 30 days and the current wording permits outright destruction of our data (walk-away territory), this fails the fallback on a material term. We propose a narrow insert (new Section 11.4) requiring return within 30 days in a machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification, together with the preferred six-month transition assistance at then-current rates; the assistance period can drop to 90 days as a fallback.

Original paragraphs:

Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.

Corio shall be responsible for providing its Customers with routine technical support of the Software and MarketSite.net Service. Corio shall escalate any technical support questions or problems it is unable to answer or resolve directly to Commerce One for Commerce One's immediate attention and resolution under the schedule set forth in EXHIBIT C hereto. The support described in this Section 5.3 and EXHIBIT C hereto shall be provided to Corio but Commerce One shall have no obligation to provide any maintenance or support services to other third parties. MINCOMMIT is satisfied at the **preferred** position: there is no minimum purchase commitment, volume quota, or take-or-pay obligation on Corio anywhere in the Agreement.

What I checked and why it doesn't bite:

Rule:

Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Finding rationale:
The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, volume quota or take-or-pay obligation on Corio, so it meets the preferred position that fees are payable only for usage or ordered services. Exhibit D's sales and marketing items are expressly "non-binding," and the initial-customers item (p0205) is only a commercially reasonable efforts undertaking, not a purchase or volume commitment. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software licence, hosting and MarketSite.net agreement  
**Status:** 19 rules assessed — 12 compliant, 6 deviations, 1 missing

---

## 1. Executive summary

On balance this is a favourable paper for us. The commercial framework carries no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment, no non-solicit and no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; the audit right in Section 4.4 is at the preferred position (annual cap, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, Vendor-borne costs with a 5% underpayment shift, no systems access); assignment is mutual with an express M&A carve-out for us; renewal is annual on 30 days' notice; and governing law sits at the fallback (California law, San Francisco-seated AAA arbitration).

The Vendor IP indemnity in Section 8 is strong and, because Section 9 excepts Section 8 from both the cap and the consequential-damages waiver, it is uncapped and one-way in our favour. Nothing there needs narrowing.

Six items require negotiation, two of which we treat as walk-away issues. First, the Section 9 cap is not twelve months' fees but only amounts actually paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to," which slices the cap to a single transaction's fees and leaves confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct inside the cap. Second, the exit provisions in Section 11.3 permit destruction of our data at the Vendor's election, with no return obligation, format, deadline or certification. Alongside those, Section 13.5 assigns ownership of Developments we create back to the Vendor wherever the Vendor supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back; the Section 2 licences do not reach our affiliates or contractors; there is no customer termination-for-convenience right in a five-year term; the product warranty period expires 60 days from the Effective Date (hard-capped at 31 December 1999) and can lapse on or before acceptance; and there is no Vendor insurance obligation anywhere in the document.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | **Deviation** | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant (fallback) | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4 FEES. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | PRICING |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4 FEES. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |

### Deviation detail and proposed positions

- **§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES (IP, critical).** Section 13.5 correctly gives us ownership of Developments created solely by us, but the "unless supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" carve-out transfers ownership of our own work product to the Vendor with no licence back. That fails both the preferred and the fallback position. *Proposal:* delete the carve-out only, leaving the Vendor's pre-existing materials and Section 2.8 Software ownership untouched; if ongoing support is the real concern, a support licence to the Vendor is the sensible fallback. Noted, not flagged: ownership of Software enhancements is left to future negotiation and there is no Customer Data ownership sentence (the Agreement has no Customer Data concept).

- **§ 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY (LOL-CAP, critical).** The clause is mutual in form and carves Section 8 out of both the cap and the consequential-damages waiver, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: the cap is limited to amounts actually paid for the single "transaction which the liability relates to" in the prior twelve months, and the only carve-out is Section 8 — confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. *Proposal:* mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, measured from the event giving rise to liability, plus an "Excluded Claims" definition covering Section 8 indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud. The mutual consequential-damages exclusion stays. *Drafting note:* p0092 appears to be an OCR duplicate across a page break; conform to the edited p0090.

- **§ 3 GRANT OF RIGHTS (LICENSE, high).** The grant is perpetual and irrevocable and Section 14.1 satisfies the fallback on transferability, but affiliates and contractors are nowhere addressed ("Affiliate" does not appear in the Agreement) and there is no mechanism to add them, failing the fallback. *Proposal:* new Section 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, with us responsible for their compliance. "Corio Servers" ("owned or operated by or for Corio") addresses contractor use only in part.

- **§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION (T4C, high).** We have no convenience right during the five-year initial term — Section 11.1 permits only non-renewal, Section 11.2 only breach or insolvency. *Proposal:* insert a Corio convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid recurring fees and no early-termination penalty, and confirm no Vendor convenience right during the term (the Vendor's lack of a mid-term right is acceptable to us). Insert after 11.2; existing 11.3 renumbers.

- **§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION (TRANSITION, medium).** Continuity is better than preferred (Sections 11.3 and 5.3 survive termination for then-existing Customers, plus Section 12 escrow), but there is no data return: Section 11.3 allows "return or destroy" at the Vendor's election, with no obligation covering our, our Customers' or Software Users' data on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no deadline and no deletion certification. *Proposal:* new Section 11.4 requiring return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification, plus six months' transition assistance at then-current rates (90 days acceptable as fallback).

- **§ 8 / 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER (WARRANTY, medium).** Sections 7.3–7.4 contain a genuine conformance, media and no-malicious-code warranty with correction, replacement and refund remedies, and the disclaimer does not swallow them. The failure is duration: 60 days from the Effective Date, hard-capped at 31 December 1999, while Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 may itself run to 31 December 1999 — so the warranty can expire on or before acceptance, below the 90-day software fallback. *Proposal:* twelve months from acceptance (preferred); 90 days from acceptance acceptable. Remedies and exclusions untouched.

- **§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS (INSURANCE, low — missing).** No insurance obligation exists; the sole use of "insurance" is an accounting exclusion in the Net Revenue definition. Absence of any coverage for a vendor whose service touches Customer data fails even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). *Proposal:* insert the preferred coverage package as new Section 14.10 and renumber Complete Understanding to 14.11.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Transaction-limited liability cap (§ 9).** A cap measured only against the fees paid for the single related transaction can fall well below six months' fees — walk-away territory for a vendor cap. We need the mutual twelve-month/USD 1,000,000 floor and the Excluded Claims carve-outs.
2. **Vendor election to destroy our data on exit (§ 11.3).** Wording that permits outright destruction with no return right is walk-away territory. We need return within 30 days in machine-readable format before any deletion, with certification.

The Section 13.5 ownership carve-out is not labelled walk-away but is a critical deviation: it assigns IP we create to the Vendor with no licence back, and we should treat it as non-negotiable in substance.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the six deviations and the missing insurance clause, prefixing each comment with **[Playbook]** and citing the playbook position and fallback.
2. Lead the negotiation on the two walk-away items (§ 9 cap and carve-outs; § 11 data return) and on § 13.5 ownership; hold the § 2 affiliate/contractor extension, § 11 convenience right and § 7 warranty duration as the second tier, where the stated fallbacks (support licence to Vendor; 90 days' transition assistance; 90 days' warranty from acceptance) give us landing zones.
3. Confirm with the business the operational impact of the five-year term without a convenience right, and the identity of the affiliates and contractors that need licence coverage.
4. Ask the Vendor for current certificates of insurance in support of the new Section 14.10.
5. On conforming the execution copy, reconcile the apparent OCR duplication at p0092 against the edited § 9 text at p0090, and renumber § 11.3 and § 14.10 as noted.
6. No action required on the compliant items; we will not spend capital on the noted sub-preferred mechanics (renewal reminder and price-uplift cap, "reasonable notice" in § 4.4, California law and arbitral forum, absence of an express affiliate carve-out and "not unreasonably withheld" qualifier in § 14.1).
"}
